name: Forster's Tern (Breeding)
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Stout orange bill with sharp black tip, solid black cap down to bill, frosty silvery-white outer primaries (paler than mantle), deeply forked tail with white outer webs, orange-red legs
photo_caption: Field profile: Orange bill with black tip, pristine white breast and belly, frosty silvery-white wingtips, long tail streamers
crux_caption: Head closeup: Orange bill base contrasting with distinct black tip, solid velvet black cap down to lower eye level

diagnostics.mark: Bright orange bill with a distinct black tip; noticeably stouter and heavier-based than Common Tern.
Outer primary flight feathers are frosted silvery-white on the upper surface, appearing paler than the back (never a dark wedge).
Pure snow-white breast and belly; deeply forked tail where outer webs are white and inner webs are gray (reverse of Common Tern).

rule_out: Orange bill with black tip + frosted silvery outer primaries + pure white underparts = Breeding Forster's Tern.

name: Forster's Tern (Fall / Non-Breeding)
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Distinctive black 'comma' or bandit eye-mask through eye, pure white nape and crown (no dark band across back of head), all-black bill, frosty silvery mantle and primaries
photo_caption: Field profile: Isolated jet-black comma eye patch surrounded by stark white head and nape, dark bill, silvery-gray back
crux_caption: Head closeup: Diagnostic isolated black eye-mask ending sharply behind eye; nape and hindneck remain entirely pure white

diagnostics.mark: Bold black comma-shaped mask through the eye that terminates behind ear coverts; nape and crown are entirely clean white.
All-black or black with faint dull reddish tinge at the extreme base during late fall/winter.
Frosty silvery-white outer primaries lacking a dark carpal bar along the leading wing edge.

rule_out: Isolated black comma eye patch + completely white nape + frosty primaries = Non-Breeding Forster's Tern.

name: Royal Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Large crested tern, massive stout carrot-orange bill, shaggy rear black crest, bald white forehead extending far back onto crown, pale gray mantle, black legs
photo_caption: Beach flock view: Huge carrot-orange bill, shaggy black crest, extensive white forehead, pure white underparts
crux_caption: Head closeup: Massive, slightly decurved carrot-orange bill and shaggy crest; forehead is cleanly white to mid-crown

diagnostics.mark: Massive, stout carrot-orange to yellowish-orange dagger bill, slightly decurved along culmen.
In almost all plumages seen post-spring, forehead is stark white extending back to mid-crown, leaving a shaggy black rear crest.
Underside of outer primaries is translucent whitish with only narrow dark tips (never solid blackish like Caspian).

rule_out: Massive carrot-orange bill + extensive white forehead + shaggy black rear crest + pale underwing = Royal Tern.

name: Common Tern (Breeding)
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Slender blood-red to coral-red bill with black tip, solid black cap, dusky grayish wash across breast/belly contrasting with white cheeks, dark translucent wedge on outer primaries
photo_caption: Field profile: Coral-red bill with black tip, pale smoky-gray underparts, sharp black cap, deeply forked tail with dark outer streamers
crux_caption: Head & bill: Coral-red bill with crisp black tip, slender tapered bill profile, duskier throat/breast than Forster's

diagnostics.mark: Slender coral-red to blood-red bill with black tip; breast and belly have an unmistakable smoky-gray wash.
Upper outer primaries show a dark grayish wedge that becomes translucent when backlit in flight.
Outer webs of outermost tail streamers are dark grayish-black (contrasting with white inner webs).

rule_out: Coral-red bill with black tip + smoky gray breast + dark primary wedge + dark outer tail webs = Breeding Common Tern.

name: Common Tern (Fall / Non-Breeding)
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Black bill, dark blackish-gray nape band connecting continuously across back of head from ear to ear, white forehead, prominent dark carpal bar on leading edge of inner wing
photo_caption: Field view: Dark nape band wrapping behind head, white forehead, dark carpal shoulder bar, black bill
crux_caption: Head & nape: Dark eye mask extends continuously across the nape (forming a solid dark collar, unlike Forster's isolated comma)

diagnostics.mark: Dark eye mask connects continuously across the nape/hindneck, forming a complete dark horseshoe/band around back of head.
Prominent dark brownish-black bar along the leading edge (carpal joint) of the inner wing (never present on adult Forster's).
Outer primaries are dusky gray to blackish (darker than inner wing, never frosty white).

rule_out: Continuous dark nape band connecting across hindneck + dark carpal bar on wing + dark primaries = Non-Breeding Common Tern.

name: Caspian Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: World's largest tern (gull-sized), massive thick blood-red bill with dark dusky tip, full black cap (finely streaked white in fall), shallow notched tail, solid blackish underwing primary patch
photo_caption: Field view: Huge bulky gull-like structure, deep coral/blood-red bill with dark smudge, full black cap, shallow tail fork
crux_caption: Head & bill: Massive heavy blood-red bill with dark subterminal smudge, black cap extending down to lower eye rim

diagnostics.mark: Massive, gull-sized body; huge, thick blood-red to deep coral bill with a dark dusky smudge near tip.
Underside of outer primaries shows an extensive, solid dusky-black wedge/patch (boldly contrasting in flight).
Full black cap (streaked white on forehead in winter, but never bald white like Royal); shallowly notched tail.

rule_out: Massive gull size + huge blood-red bill with dark tip + solid blackish underwing patch = Caspian Tern.

name: Least Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Tiny petite structure (smallest NA tern), bright yellow bill with sharp black tip, stark white triangular forehead patch against black cap, bright yellow legs, buoyant fluttery flight
photo_caption: Beach nesting profile: Tiny size, yellow bill with black tip, white forehead chevron, yellow legs
crux_caption: Head closeup: Crisp white forehead triangle contrasting with jet-black cap and black lores line, yellow bill

diagnostics.mark: Smallest North American tern (only 8.5-9 inches); quick, buoyant, erratic swallow-like wingbeats.
Bright yellow bill with a sharp black tip; prominent stark white triangular patch on forehead.
Short, bright yellow to orange-yellow legs (all other small/medium Sterna have reddish or black legs).

rule_out: Tiny size + yellow bill with black tip + white triangular forehead patch + yellow legs = Least Tern.

name: Black Skimmer
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Bizarre knife-like laterally compressed red-and-black bill with lower mandible far longer than upper, jet-black upperparts, snow-white face and underparts, bright reddish-orange legs
photo_caption: Field profile: Unique knife bill, black cap and back, white underparts, long pointed black wings
crux_caption: Bill closeup: Massive knife-thin red bill base with jet black tip; lower mandible extends significantly beyond upper mandible

diagnostics.mark: Huge laterally compressed blade-like bill; lower mandible is up to an inch longer than upper mandible for water-skimming.
Solid jet-black crown, nape, back, and wings; brilliant pure snow-white forehead, cheeks, and underparts.
Flies low over calm water with lower mandible cutting the surface, snapping shut on contact with fish.

rule_out: Blade-like red bill with elongated lower mandible + black back + white underparts = Black Skimmer.

name: Black Tern (Breeding)
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Small marsh tern, entirely jet-black head, neck, breast, and belly, contrasting slate-gray mantle and wings, crisp white undertail coverts, small black bill, dark legs
photo_caption: Perched marsh profile: Solid soot-black head and underparts, slate-gray wings, white vent, erratic flight
crux_caption: Field view: Jet-black underparts contrasting sharply with pure white undertail coverts and silver-gray underwing lining

diagnostics.mark: Solid velvety soot-black head, neck, breast, and belly (completely unique among North American terns).
Contrasting medium slate-gray mantle and wings; short, shallowly notched gray tail with crisp white undertail coverts.
Small, delicate marsh tern with fluttery butterfly-like flight, dipping to pick insects from water and marshes.

rule_out: Solid soot-black head and body + slate-gray wings + white undertail = Breeding Black Tern.

name: Black Tern (Fall / Non-Breeding)
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Small delicate build, white underparts and head, dark blackish-gray cap with dark ear spot, diagnostic dark smudge on side of white breast in front of wing bend, pale gray back
photo_caption: Fall field view: White head and underparts, dark cap, diagnostic dark chest smudge at shoulder, fluttery flight
crux_caption: Chest closeup: Diagnostic downward dark gray spur/smudge on side of breast in front of folded wing bend

diagnostics.mark: Dark dusky gray vertical patch/smudge extending downward on the side of the white breast just in front of the wing bend.
White face and throat with a dark grayish-black cap that connects to an ear spot behind the eye.
Tiny, delicate marsh tern structure with short shallowly notched tail and slender needle-sharp black bill.

rule_out: Tiny marsh tern + white underparts with dark side-breast smudge + dark cap/ear spot = Non-Breeding Black Tern.

name: Gull-billed Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Stout gull-like structure, heavy thick stubby black bill (gull-like, blunt, not needle-sharp), full black cap, pale silver-gray mantle, pure white underparts, long black legs
photo_caption: Field profile: Unmistakable thick stubby black bill, sturdy body, broad rounded wings, long black legs
crux_caption: Bill closeup: Heavy, thick, blunt black bill lacking needle-sharp tip; hunts insects and crabs over saltmarshes

diagnostics.mark: Exceptionally thick, heavy, stubby black bill; blunt and gull-like rather than long and needle-sharp.
Broader, more rounded wings and shorter, less deeply forked tail than typical Sterna terns.
Hawks insects over marshes and plucks fiddler crabs from mudflats; rarely or never plunge-dives into open water.

rule_out: Heavy, thick stubby black gull-like bill + pale plumage + insect-hawking marsh flight = Gull-billed Tern.

name: Sandwich Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Slender crested tern, long slender black bill with a sharply defined lemon-yellow tip, shaggy black crest on back of crown, pale gray mantle, white underparts, black legs with yellow soles
photo_caption: Field profile: Long black bill with brilliant yellow tip, shaggy rear crest, slender build, black legs
crux_caption: Bill closeup: Sharp, narrow pencil-like black bill tipped distinctly with pale lemon-yellow

diagnostics.mark: Long, slender black bill with a sharply demarcated pale yellow to ivory tip ('pencil dipped in yellow paint').
Slender, attenuated crested tern structure with a shaggy black crest projecting from the rear crown.
Very pale, bleached silver-gray mantle and white underparts; black legs with distinctive yellowish soles.

rule_out: Long slender black bill with crisp yellow tip + shaggy black crest = Sandwich Tern.

name: Roseate Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Very pale frosty silvery-white mantle, solid black cap, all-black slender bill, exceptionally long white tail streamers extending far beyond folded wingtips at rest, red legs
photo_caption: Field profile: Extremely long white tail streamers extending well past folded wings, all-black bill, pale ghostly plumage
crux_caption: Tail & bill view: Slender black bill (red base only in late summer), streamers exceeding wingtips by 2-3 inches

diagnostics.mark: Extremely long, pure white outer tail streamers that project 2 to 3 inches beyond the folded wingtips at rest.
Slender, needle-sharp all-black bill in early summer (developing red at the extreme base only by late breeding season).
Palest of all medium terns—frosty silvery-white mantle; breast shows a delicate faint pinkish-rose blush in spring.

rule_out: Tail streamers extending far beyond wingtips at rest + all-black slender bill + frosty pale mantle = Roseate Tern.

name: Arctic Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Compact body sitting very low to ground on diagnostic exceptionally short coral-red legs, short blood-red bill (entirely red with no black tip), solid black cap, translucent primaries with thin black trailing edge
photo_caption: Field view: Extremely short legs (sits nearly flat on ground), short blood-red bill with no black, white cheek stripe
crux_caption: Head & bill: Short, slender, all-red bill without black tip, crisp white cheek line separating black cap from gray throat

diagnostics.mark: Diagnostic exceptionally short legs (tarsus only 15-16 mm); bird stands very low and appears to sit on its belly.
Short, delicate, deep blood-red bill with NO black tip whatsoever (contrast with Common and Forster's).
All primaries are uniform translucent white when backlit in flight, edged beneath with a narrow, crisp pencil-thin black line.

rule_out: Exceptionally short legs + all-red short bill with no black tip + translucent flight feathers = Arctic Tern.

name: Sooty Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Stark jet-black upperparts (crown, nape, back, and wings), pure crisp snow-white underparts, white forehead patch ending strictly before the eye, deeply forked tail with white outer margins, black bill and legs
photo_caption: Pelagic view: Pitch-black upperparts contrasting with pure snow-white underparts, white forehead triangle, black bill
crux_caption: Face pattern: White forehead patch ends sharply in front of eye (does NOT extend past eye into an eyebrow)

diagnostics.mark: Stark, pitch-black crown, nape, back, and wings sharply contrasting with pristine snow-white underparts.
White triangular forehead patch ends squarely BEFORE the eye; black lores line connects directly to dark eye.
Long, deeply forked tail with prominent white outer margins; oceanic pelagic wanderer brought by tropical storms.

rule_out: Jet-black back + pure white underparts + white forehead ending before eye = Sooty Tern.

name: Bridled Tern
plate_caption: Diagnostic plate: Dark smoky grayish-brown mantle and wings (not jet black), black cap separated from mantle by a distinct pale whitish collar across the hindneck, white forehead patch extending as a narrow white eyebrow past the eye, white underparts
photo_caption: Pelagic profile: Brownish-gray back, distinct white collar on hindneck, white eyebrow extending behind eye, black bill
crux_caption: Head closeup: White forehead continues backward as a distinct narrow white supercilium trailing past the eye

diagnostics.mark: Distinct pale whitish collar on the nape and hindneck cleanly separating the black cap from the dark mantle.
White forehead continues as a narrow white stripe (eyebrow) extending backward beyond the eye (the 'bridle').
Upperparts are dark smoky grayish-brown, visibly paler and browner than the solid jet-black of Sooty Tern.

rule_out: Smoky brown back + white collar on hindneck + white eyebrow extending past eye = Bridled Tern.
